title: The Lie Who Moved In
caption: The Lie Who Moved In 🤥 An animated story about a town where every lie turns into a person. What lie would follow you home? #animatedstory #storytime #blockmated

shots.text: In my town, every lie you tell turns into a person.
And they'll do anything to make it true.
Little lies are little. About the size of a cat.
They sit under the desks and agree with everything you say.
Benny once told everybody he wasn't scared of the dark.
Now a tiny blue Benny sleeps under his bed and holds his hand all night.
Big lies are big.
Rafi told his mom he cleaned his room. His lie is taller than the lockers.
Pip has never told a lie. Not once. Not even to be nice.
And nobody knows whose lie Mr. Bramble is.
He moved in the day I was born. Nobody saw him arrive.
On Monday, Ms. Graves asked if I'd done my homework.
I said yes.
Something tapped my shoe.
A tiny blue me, holding a pencil, smiling way too much.
He followed me home.
That night, he did my homework.
Every single answer was yes.
What's seven times eight? Yes.
What's the capital of France? Yes.
Ms. Graves asked why every answer was yes. I said my dog ate my real homework.
We don't have a dog.
My lie grew a foot taller. That's the thing about lies.
Every lie you tell to protect one feeds it.
By Wednesday, he was as tall as me.
He answered roll call. He ate my lunch. Ms. Graves didn't even blink.
By Thursday, he was taller than Ms. Graves.
And he'd started calling my mom, Mom.
Mom just said, set an extra plate.
I tried locking him in the closet.
He was already in my bed. In my pajamas.
Pip said by Friday, he wouldn't need me anymore.
But Pip has never lied, so she's the only one who knows how they work.
A lie only leaves when the person you lied to hears the truth.
So on Friday, I stood up in front of the whole class,
with a giant smiling me right behind me.
And I told Ms. Graves the truth. I didn't do my homework.
Not on Monday. Not ever.
He shrank like a balloon,
down to the size of a cat. He waved at me. Then he was gone.
And for the first time ever, Ms. Graves blinked.
That night, I told Mom everything.
She hugged me for a long time. Then she told me a secret.
The day I was born, she held me and whispered, everything is going to be fine.
Mr. Bramble moved in the next morning.
He's been making it true ever since.
